unit: BTEC IT Level 3 Unit 4 - Relational Database Development

A.title: Understand how the principles of relational database models, data storage and normalisation are used to create effective relational database solutions

topics.name: Relational database management systems
keyPoints: Types of RDBMS: desktop databases (e.g. Microsoft Access — single file, local, one user at a time) and server databases (MySQL, Oracle — central server, many concurrent users)
Relational data structure concepts: relation (table), attribute (column), domain (allowed values), tuple (row), degree (number of columns), cardinality (number of rows)
Relational algebra operations: union, intersect, join and select
Relational keys: super key, candidate key, primary key, foreign key
Integrity constraints: entity integrity (PK never null/duplicate) and referential integrity (FK must match an existing PK or be null)
Entity relationship types: one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many

topics.name: Manipulating data structures and data
keyPoints: Defining, modifying and removing data structures and data (CREATE, ALTER, DROP)
Updating, inserting, modifying and deleting data (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE)
Retrieval of data for queries and reports (SELECT with criteria, sorting, grouping)

topics.name: Normalisation
keyPoints: Purpose: develop efficient data structures free of redundancy and dependency problems
Anomalies: update, insertion and deletion anomalies caused by poor table design
Keys: primary, foreign and composite keys
Referential integrity and the data dictionary
Stages: un-normalised form (UNF) → first (1NF) → second (2NF) → third normal form (3NF)
1NF removes repeating groups (atomic values); 2NF removes partial dependencies; 3NF removes transitive dependencies

topics.name: Preliminary scoping of a solution in response to a client brief
keyPoints: Purpose: the problem to be solved and the technical requirements
Research: existing databases, structuring data into tables and keys, available resources
Use accurate technical vocabulary and plan the logical structure

B.title: Design a relational database solution to meet client requirements

topics.name: Relational database design techniques and processes
keyPoints: Entity relationship modelling: conceptual (entities + relationships) and logical (adds attributes, primary keys, foreign keys)
Relational algebra: one-to-many, one-to-one, many-to-many; AND, OR, NOT, >, <, >=, <=
DBMS selection: desktop software vs cloud/server-based
Database implementation techniques: prototyping and testing
Quality and appropriateness: correctness of data, relationships, data integrity, normalisation

topics.name: Design documentation
keyPoints: Design specification: requirements of the brief, audience, purpose, client requirements, legal and ethical considerations (data protection legislation, regulations)
Data structure designs: data dictionaries (tables, field names, lengths, data types, validation), ERDs, normalisation

User interface design: forms (input/calculated/disabled fields, combo boxes, list boxes, radio buttons, validation, masks, user help), menus (action buttons), queries (multiple criteria, form values, wildcards, action queries, calculated queries), reports (calculated fields, grouping, layouts, conditional formatting), task automation (macros, scripts, code)
Test plans: data integrity, functionality, accessibility, usability
Implementation plan and timescales

topics.name: Reviewing and refining designs
keyPoints: Self-review against: suitability for user, meeting client requirements, legal and ethical constraints, consistency
Refine ideas and solutions, then update the design specification documentation

C.title: Develop a relational database solution to meet client requirements

topics.name: Producing a database solution
keyPoints: Use an appropriate DBMS and SQL to create, set up and maintain data tables
Create links/relationships between tables and apply validation rules
Generate outputs: user-generated queries, automated queries, reports
Build the user interface: navigation, data entry forms, child (sub) forms
Task automation, and populating the database by importing, adding and manipulating data

topics.name: Testing the database solution
keyPoints: Testing types: referential integrity and functionality
Test data: erroneous, extreme and normal
Object testing: tables, queries, reports, forms, menus
Usability testing: selecting suitable test users and devising suitable tests
Gather feedback, produce test documentation, and use outcomes to refine the solution

topics.name: Reviewing the database solution
keyPoints: Review against: quality of the database, fitness for purpose, suitability against original requirements, legal and ethical constraints, strengths and improvements

topics.name: Optimising the database solution
keyPoints: Data types and data sizes (size on disk, image storage requirements)
Many tables: overheads and query complexity
Query optimisation: select specific columns, efficient joins/sub-queries
